summary.intent: Execute Phase 19.2 (IPFS upload performance optimization) gap closure, collect matched-environment load test baselines to validate SDK concurrent pin and Kubo pebbleds datastore optimizations, then create and review a PR.
summary.outcome: All 4 Phase 19.2 plans completed and verified. Three-point local baseline comparison collected at 50 clients (matching environment). Concurrent SDK pins alone regress performance at 50 clients; combined with pebbleds they deliver p95 -13%, p99 -15%, throughput +7%. A bonus 75-client run showed pebbleds eliminates the failure mode entirely (0 errors vs 10, p95 -53%). PR #342 created, reviewed, and cleaned up.

repo: SDK concurrent pins and pebbleds datastore are synergistic — concurrent pins alone overwhelm flatfs at 50 clients (p95 blows up from 18.7s to 44.7s), but combined with pebbleds they improve all metrics.

Rate limiting is bypassed via two env vars: LOAD_TEST_SECRET (sent to POST /auth/test-login) and THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET (sent as X-Throttle-Bypass header). These must be passed inline as shell env vars — vitest does not use dotenv.
Active CIDs tracked in two DB tables: `pinned_cids` (file content) and `folder_ipns` (metadata blobs where latest_cid IS NOT NULL). Anything pinned on Kubo not in these tables is stale.
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL in apps/api/.env was pointing to localhost:3001 (mock-ipns-routing); someguy on 192.168.133.114:8190 should be used for staging-representative testing.
Load test SDK client checkout points for pre/post optimization: pre-optimization parent is 4087fa2b6^, post-SDK-only is 565dccd5d, post-pebbleds is HEAD.
NODE_ENV=test in apps/api/.env relaxes throttle limits; THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET via header fully bypasses regardless of client count.
All three SDK test files (client.test.ts, client-extended.test.ts, client-upload-concurrency.test.ts) had identical createTestConfig helper — extracted to packages/sdk/src/__tests__/helpers.ts.

code.finding: uploadFile now uses Promise.allSettled to parallelize IPNS publish and folder metadata update. On partial failure, emits a new 'upload:batchPublishFailed' event (consistent with 'share:reWrapFailed' pattern) in addition to console.warn.
Added 'upload:batchPublishFailed' typed event for when concurrent pin batch partially fails — keeps event taxonomy consistent with existing error events.
New file — shared createTestConfig and setupFolder helpers extracted from three test files to eliminate copy-paste duplication.
setTimeout(r, 10) replaced with Promise.resolve() for async tick in tests — faster and semantically equivalent for yielding to the microtask queue.

workflow: When comparing optimizations, keep the environment identical across all runs — staging vs localhost with different client counts makes the comparison non-definitive.
A concurrency probe run (Run 0) at increasing client counts is valuable before committing to a baseline client count — reveals the knee and failure modes.

For staging datastore migrations, parallel cutover (spin up new container alongside old, cross-reference CIDs against DB to skip stale ones, copy volume, swap) is safer than clean slate when data matters.
Kubo flatfs→pebbleds is not a standard ipfs repo migrate path — requires manual volume copy or ipfs-ds-convert rather than built-in migration.
Running multiple pnpm dev processes in background accumulates zombie wrappers; only one can hold the port but the others consume resources silently.

friction: API was not running when load tests started — had to start it manually mid-workflow.
Three duplicate API processes accumulated from background starts; required manual PID hunting and force kills.
SDK checkout for pre-optimization baseline required manual git checkout from tests/load working directory, which caused the restore to fail silently until the directory issue was identified.
Vitest does not load dotenv, so LOAD_TEST_SECRET and THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET must be passed inline — not obvious from the test setup.
Background task completion notifications for already-captured results arrived late and cluttered the conversation.
Web frontend process was killed by the earlier process cleanup, requiring restart.
19.2-04 plan had to be replanned twice: once for the three-point local approach (vs staging), and again to capture the exact run commands, secrets, and someguy config before execution.
open_items: Staging pebbleds migration: parallel cutover procedure needs to be performed manually on 192.168.133.114 — PR #342 merged, but staging deploy + IPFS volume migration not yet done.
